definitions.explanation: A reason given to justify or explain one's actions, often implying it may not be entirely valid.
An attempt to explain the circumstances behind something.

examples.japanese: {遅刻|ちこく}の{言|い}い{訳|わけ}ばかりするな。
examples.english: Stop making excuses for being late.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}の{言|い}い{訳|わけ}は{信|しん}じられない。
{言|い}い{訳|わけ}をする{暇|ひま}があったら{行動|こうどう}しろ。
examples.english: Instead of making excuses, take action.

examples.japanese: {事情|じじょう}を{言|い}い{訳|わけ}した。
{言|い}い{訳|わけ}を{聞|き}いてください。
{彼女|かのじょ}は{自分|じぶん}の{立場|たちば}を{言|い}い{訳|わけ}するために{長|なが}い{手紙|てがみ}を{書|か}いた。
examples.english: She wrote a long letter to explain her position.

notes:
{言|い}い{訳|わけ} often carries a negative nuance, implying the reason may not be genuine.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {言|い}い{訳|わけ}をする - to make an excuse
- {言|い}い{訳|わけ}にならない - is no excuse
- {言|い}い{訳|わけ}ばかり - nothing but excuses
- {言|い}い{訳|わけ}{無用|むよう} - no excuses accepted

NUANCE:
{言|い}い{訳|わけ} typically implies the speaker is trying to avoid responsibility or make themselves look better, whereas {説明|せつめい} (explanation) is more neutral.

RELATED EXPRESSIONS:
- {言|い}い{訳|わけ}がましい - excuse-making, overly apologetic
- {屁理屈|へりくつ} - sophistry, specious argument

SURU-VERB USAGE:
{言|い}い{訳|わけ}する can be used as a verb meaning "to make excuses."
